---
title: "Gene-set contrasts: HR against LR"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    toc: true
execute:
  echo: true
  warning: false
---

Single proteins carry little HR-against-LR signal at this sample size; sets pool many weak shifts.
Every gene set is tested in the nine contrasts by two methods that ask different questions, with
FDR controlled within each database. The step ends by choosing, per window, the sets the pathway
figure draws, grouping near-duplicates into a tree.

## Packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(limma)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
source(here("02_HRvLR", "helpers.R"))
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
inputs <- c(
  gene_sets = "01_Processing/04_Gene_Sets/c_data/gene_sets.rds",
  fit = "02_HRvLR/01_Protein_Contrasts/c_data/fit.rds",
  set_scores = "01_Processing/05_Set_Scores/c_data/singscore.rds"
)
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
```

## Input

The gene sets (one protein per gene, disease sets excluded) and the protein fit.

```{r}
#| label: input
gs <- readRDS(paths[["gene_sets"]])
saved <- readRDS(paths[["fit"]])
eb <- saved$eb
contrasts <- colnames(saved$contrast_matrix)
catalog <- filter(gs$set_catalog, qualifies)
sets <- gs$sets[catalog$set_id]
count(catalog, collection)
```

## What each method receives

fgsea ranks every protein by its moderated t in one contrast and asks whether a set's proteins sit
nearer the top or bottom than chance (normalised enrichment score, NES). fry asks whether a set's
proteins move together across people in that contrast, using the same design and person block as
the protein fit. fgsea needs genes, so each representative protein is named by its gene.

```{r}
#| label: method-inputs
chosen <- filter(gs$protein_map, selected)
ranked <- map(set_names(contrasts), \(cn) {
  set_names(eb$t[chosen$uniprot_id, cn], chosen$gene)
})
set_rows <- map(sets, \(genes) match(chosen$uniprot_id[match(genes, chosen$gene)], rownames(eb)))
stopifnot(!any(map_lgl(set_rows, anyNA)))
lengths(sets) |> summary()
```

## Tests, FDR within each database

fgsea estimates p by permutation, so it is seeded. When a contrast's statistics lean one way, fgsea
cannot estimate p for some sets and leaves p, NES and FDR missing; `nPermSimple = 10000` keeps those
few, and they are listed below. fry has no such limit. Both methods run one database at a time, so
each `fdr` is Benjamini-Hochberg within one database and one contrast.

```{r}
#| label: tests
set.seed(1)
by_db <- split(catalog$set_id, catalog$collection)
fgsea_tests <- expand_grid(contrast = contrasts, collection = names(by_db)) |>
  pmap(\(contrast, collection) {
    fgsea::fgsea(sets[by_db[[collection]]], ranked[[contrast]],
      minSize = 15, maxSize = 500, nPermSimple = 10000
    ) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      transmute(
        contrast, collection, set_id = pathway, method = "fgsea", n_proteins = size,
        nes = NES, p = pval, fdr = padj, leading_edge = leadingEdge
      )
  }) |>
  list_rbind()
fry_tests <- expand_grid(contrast = contrasts, collection = names(by_db)) |>
  pmap(\(contrast, collection) {
    fry(saved$fit$EList,
      index = set_rows[by_db[[collection]]], design = saved$design,
      contrast = saved$contrast_matrix[, contrast], block = saved$fit$EList$targets$subject,
      correlation = saved$fit$correlation, sort = "none"
    ) |>
      as_tibble(rownames = "set_id") |>
      transmute(
        contrast, collection, set_id, method = "fry", n_proteins = NGenes,
        direction = Direction, p = PValue, fdr = FDR
      )
  }) |>
  list_rbind()
set_tests <- bind_rows(fgsea_tests, fry_tests) |>
  left_join(select(catalog, set_id, pathway), by = "set_id")
set_tests |>
  filter(is.na(p)) |>
  select(contrast, collection, pathway, n_proteins)
set_tests |>
  summarise(n_fdr_05 = sum(fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(method, contrast)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = n_fdr_05)
```

## Sets for the pathway figure

The figure groups the nine contrasts into four windows. A set is a candidate for the training or
acute window when fgsea calls it at FDR < 0.05 in HR, in LR or in both, and that call places it in a
block: shared, HR only or LR only. Between groups, a set needs FDR < 0.05 at two of the three time
points; in the interaction window, in either interaction. GO Slim is left out: its broad terms
repeat GO:BP.

A set in the HR-only block passed in HR and missed in LR. That alone does not show HR changed it
more; the interaction contrast tests that, so each training and acute candidate also records
whether its window's interaction reaches FDR < 0.05. Within a block, candidates rank by whether
their calls agree in sign, then by that interaction, then by their smallest p.

```{r}
#| label: candidates
windows <- list(
  Training = c("Training_HR", "Training_LR"), Acute = c("Acute_HR", "Acute_LR"),
  `HR - LR` = c("Baseline_HRvLR", "Trained_HRvLR", "Acute_HRvLR"),
  Interaction = c("Training_Interaction", "Acute_Interaction")
)
needed <- c(Training = 1, Acute = 1, `HR - LR` = 2, Interaction = 1)
gsea_main <- filter(fgsea_tests, collection != "GO_Slim")
calls <- with(filter(gsea_main, fdr < 0.05), paste(contrast, set_id))
is_called <- \(contrast, set_id) paste(contrast, set_id) %in% calls
within_group <- c("Training", "Acute")
candidates <- imap(windows, \(cns, win) {
  gsea_main |>
    filter(contrast %in% cns) |>
    summarise(
      n_proteins = first(n_proteins), hits = sum(fdr < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
      same_sign = n_distinct(sign(nes[which(fdr < 0.05)])) == 1,
      best_p = min(p[which(fdr < 0.05)], Inf), .by = c(set_id, collection)
    ) |>
    filter(hits >= needed[[win]]) |>
    mutate(window = win)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(
    in_hr = is_called(paste0(window, "_HR"), set_id),
    in_lr = is_called(paste0(window, "_LR"), set_id),
    pattern = case_when(
      !window %in% within_group ~ NA_character_,
      in_hr & in_lr ~ "shared", in_hr ~ "HR only", .default = "LR only"
    ),
    interaction = if_else(
      window %in% within_group, is_called(paste0(window, "_Interaction"), set_id), NA
    ),
    block = if_else(is.na(pattern), window, paste0(window, ": ", pattern))
  ) |>
  select(-in_hr, -in_lr) |>
  arrange(desc(same_sign), desc(interaction), best_p) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(), .by = block)
count(candidates, window, block)
```

Overlapping sets are grouped, not dropped. Within each block, sets are clustered by the proteins
they share (Jaccard similarity: shared ÷ union; average linkage), as EnrichmentMap and DAVID group
them (Merico et al. 2010; Huang et al. 2007), and the tree is cut at three heights; at 0.85, sets
in one cluster share on average at least about 15% of their proteins. Each cluster is shown by its
most specific set: the smallest whose p is within 10-fold of the cluster's best, so a narrow set
nested in a broad one takes its place when the evidence is close. The main figure draws the
representatives at 0.85; the supplement draws every candidate beside its tree, and the cuts at 0.75
and 0.9.

```{r}
#| label: tree
selection <- candidates |>
  group_by(block) |>
  group_modify(\(d, key) set_tree(d, sets)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    representative_0.75 = most_specific(cut_0.75, best_p, n_proteins),
    representative_0.85 = most_specific(cut_0.85, best_p, n_proteins),
    representative_0.9 = most_specific(cut_0.9, best_p, n_proteins), .by = block
  ) |>
  relocate(window, block, pattern, .before = 1) |>
  arrange(match(window, names(windows)), block, rank)
selection |>
  summarise(
    candidates = n(), interaction = sum(interaction), across(starts_with("representative"), sum),
    .by = c(window, block)
  )
```

## Validation

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(filter(set_tests, method == "fry")$p), all(set_tests$fdr >= set_tests$p, na.rm = TRUE),
  all(selection$set_id %in% catalog$set_id), !any(catalog$disease_set)
)
```

## Hallmark set scores

The supplementary score heatmap (S3 e) tests the Hallmark sets with 15 to 500 measured genes (35 of
the 50) as per-biopsy singscore scores, chosen in advance rather than by the tests above. Each score goes through the eigengene fit of
`03_Module_Contrasts`: the protein design, person as a block with the within-person correlation
estimated on the scores, robust eBayes. `df` is limma's total degrees of freedom, which the heatmap
needs to turn t into an r-equivalent. `fdr` is Benjamini-Hochberg across these sets within a
contrast.

```{r}
#| label: score-tests
scores <- readRDS(paths[["set_scores"]])$scores
hallmark <- catalog$set_id[catalog$collection == "Hallmark"]
hallmark_scores <- scores[hallmark, saved$fit$EList$targets$sample_id]
score_block <- saved$fit$EList$targets$subject
score_correlation <- duplicateCorrelation(hallmark_scores, saved$design, block = score_block)
score_fit <- lmFit(hallmark_scores, saved$design,
  block = score_block, correlation = score_correlation$consensus.correlation
) |>
  contrasts.fit(saved$contrast_matrix) |>
  eBayes(robust = TRUE)
score_tests <- map(set_names(contrasts), \(cn) {
  topTable(score_fit, coef = cn, number = Inf, sort.by = "none", confint = TRUE) |>
    as_tibble(rownames = "set_id") |>
    transmute(
      set_id, logFC, logFC_lower = CI.L, logFC_upper = CI.R, t,
      df = score_fit$df.total[match(set_id, rownames(score_fit))], p = P.Value, fdr = adj.P.Val
    )
}) |>
  list_rbind(names_to = "contrast")
stopifnot(nrow(score_tests) == length(hallmark) * length(contrasts), !anyNA(score_tests$p))
length(hallmark)
c(within_person_correlation = round(score_correlation$consensus.correlation, 3))
count(filter(score_tests, fdr < 0.05), contrast)
```

## Summary

`r length(sets)` sets in `r length(by_db)` databases, tested in nine contrasts by fgsea and fry.
`r sum(selection$representative_0.85)` sets represent the clusters of the `r n_distinct(selection$block)`
blocks at cut 0.85; Figure 3 draws the first few of each block by rank.

## Save

```{r}
#| label: save
out <- here("02_HRvLR", "02_Set_Contrasts", "c_data")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(
  list(set_tests = set_tests, selection = selection, score_tests = score_tests),
  file.path(out, "set_tests.rds")
)
write_workbook(
  list(
    set_tests = mutate(set_tests,
      leading_edge = map_chr(leading_edge, \(x) paste(x, collapse = ";"))
    ),
    selection = selection, score_tests = score_tests
  ),
  c(
    "Per contrast, database and set: fgsea NES or fry direction, p and FDR within the database.",
    "Candidate sets per block: rank, tree clusters at three cuts, most specific set per cluster.",
    "Per contrast and qualifying Hallmark set: limma on the singscore set score, with df and FDR."
  ),
  file.path(out, "set_contrasts.xlsx"), inputs, paths
)
```
